title: Converge TFState boundaries and standardize GPU scheduling profiles for Private deploys
author: Maya Ortiz
description: Motivation: Private deployments have accumulated ad-hoc tfstate boundaries and heterogeneous GPU node pool configs which complicate upgrades and cross-tenant networking. This PR rationalizes state layout, adds a safe migrator workflow, and standardizes GPU taints/affinities and IAM templates. Goals: 1) Move from multiple overlapping tfstate backends to a clear per-vpc + shared-infra split while preserving rollback ability; 2) Introduce a migration tool that creates a plan-only preview and a reversible apply path; 3) Standardize GPU node pool profiles (scheduling, taints, labels) and expose those as stable variables; 4) Split IAM role module into workload-scoped templates (serving, admin, metrics) to reduce cross-scope privileges; 5) Add compact networking module for peered-private-slices used by on-prem clusters. Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] automated migrator implemented, [x] terraform validate & fmt passing, [x] staged upgrade documented, [ ] e2e migration run in staging (scheduled). Migration notes: the migrator uses temporary workspaces and creates a guard record in state to allow automated rollback. Customers with custom state layouts are supported via an opt-in mapping file (examples/legacy-mapping.tfvars).

review_comments: Jonah: Can we make the migrator idempotent if it is re-run against a partially migrated state? Suggest adding a guard file and an explicit --resume flag.
Author (Maya): Migrator now creates migration.lock in the target backend and supports --resume; added tests covering interrupted runs.
Priya: IAM split looks good, but please ensure default policy size stays under the provider limit. Consider creating a minimal service role for metrics ingestion.
Author (Maya): Pulled common policy fragments into iam/_fragments.tf and added a minimal metrics role with reduced privileges.
Evelyn: Tests failed in CI on first run (terraform fmt diff). I see a follow-up commit fixed formatting and the CI run passed.
Ops (manual comment): During staging migration, we observed elevated control-plane API calls; added rate-limit throttle to migrator and documented backoff behavior.
release_notes: Consolidated tfstate layout for Private deployments (per-vpc + shared-infra), added a reversible tfstate migrator, standardized GPU node pool scheduling and taint profiles, split IAM templates by workload type, and introduced a peered-slices networking module for on-prem VPC peering. Migration tool and guide included at docs/private-deploy-upgrade.md.
upgrade_plan: Staged rollout recommended: 1) Run migrator in preview mode against a copy of backend in staging; 2) Apply to one non-prod VPC and validate runtime (GPU scheduling, IAM role bindings); 3) Run migrator in target VPCs during a maintenance window with --throttle; 4) If issues, run migrator --rollback which restores state snapshot and removes lock. Detailed steps in docs/private-deploy-upgrade.md
testing_summary: Unit tests for migrator and module-level tf validate added. Integration staging migration run scheduled; initial smoke tests pass on nodepool creation/scale, IAM binding assertions, and peering connectivity using our perf-canary harness.
notes_for_ops: The migrator writes migration.lock to the backend and stores a timestamped snapshot (S3/GCS) before making changes. Ensure long-term backend credentials are scoped correctly; rolling back requires access to snapshot buckets. If using custom backend paths, supply examples/legacy-mapping.tfvars to map old state segments.

changelog_entry: infra: unify private tfstate layout and add migrator; standardize GPU nodepool profiles; split IAM templates
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: no automatic re-tagging of existing nodepools, only new profile variables and an explicit migrator path. Customers with highly-customized tfstate should coordinate with SRE before running migrator.
